Thanks — dug into the traces and ran a quick local repro with the attached prompt set. High-level findings and mitigations: 

Root-cause hypotheses:
1) Token buffering + per-chunk stop enforcement: when runtime flushes partial chunks, the stop-sequence can be split across boundaries leading to missed stops and continuation that degrades coherence.
2) Sampling drift under streaming: some model variants (smaller quantized variants) show higher entropy once the context window includes several doc summaries; streaming encourages earlier token emission which magnifies sampling noise.
3) Prefix KV cold starts: repeated cache misses during early streaming bursts increase latency spikes and may lead to truncated context that harms coherence.

Quick mitigations (fast to test during pairing):
- Enforce boundary-safe stop detection: use the runtime flag stream.stop_buffer=128 (keeps last 128 bytes for cross-chunk matching).
- Aggressive stop token pairing: add an explicit unique end token in the prompt (e.g., <NB_END>) in addition to newline sequences; this prevents split-token ambiguity.
- Try model variant: Mistral-Instruct-7B (non-quantized) or RedOpt-13B-q4 with higher top_p (0.92) — both maintain coherence better in our eval.
- Reduce per-token emission buffer to 16ms and enable token-level entropy smoothing (runtime.flag sample.smooth=0.6) for streaming.

Repro checklist for pairing (30m):
1) Customer provides 10 redacted docs + one failing prompt from prompt-set-v2.txt.
2) SE spins up Mistral-7B baseline with stream.stop_buffer=128 and stream.emit_delay=16ms.
3) Run 5 reps each: streaming vs non-streaming, Mistral vs RedOpt-13B-q4. Collect nb-demo-logs.jsonl-like traces.
4) Compare: token-level stop hits, hallucination score on labeled segments, median 95th latency.
5) If stop misses persist, switch to explicit <NB_END> token and re-run.
